newsitem.title: USA: Persistence pays off for California bank robber.
newsitem.headline: Persistence pays off for California bank robber.

text.p: The second time proved the charm for a brash bandit who made off with $600 from a San Francisco bank a day after his first attempt to rob the same branch was foiled, police said Thursday.

Police said the thief robbed a First Nationwide Bank branch in San Francisco on Tuesday. The teller turned over $2,400 in a bag that contained a dye sack, used as a security measure. When the dye sack exploded, the would-be robber dropped the loot and ran.

Undaunted, the man returned to the same branch on Wednesday, approached the same teller and demanded cash. The teller turned over $600 and this time the bandit got away. Police said there was no dye sack in the money on Wednesday.
Police said the robber's persistence was surprising. "We've had people do the same banks, but not two days in a row," San Francisco police inspector Tom Horan said.
Horan said he had no leads yet. But he said video from the bank may help police identify the robber.
